name: JustSupply synthetic due-diligence retrieval benchmark
description: A synthetic, non-confidential corpus for measuring multilingual evidence retrieval before changing RAG chunking and ranking settings. All organizations and events are fictional.

documents.title: Aurora Foods 2025 Workforce Development Report
documents.text:
Aurora Foods operates a fictional cocoa processing business. In 2025, women represented 52 percent of its permanent workforce and 41 percent of factory supervisors. The company recorded workforce composition by employment category rather than reporting only an organization-wide percentage.

The Women in Operations program enrolled 84 employees in technical and leadership training. Sixty-three participants completed the full course, and 18 were promoted within six months. The report does not compare promotion outcomes with a control group, so it does not establish that the program caused those promotions.

Aurora introduced sixteen weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers and six weeks for secondary caregivers. Factory employees may request adjusted shifts for six months after returning from leave. The report states that 27 employees used parental leave during the year, including 19 production workers.

The report also discloses a remaining gap: women held 29 percent of executive positions at year end. Management set a goal of reaching 40 percent by 2028, but this target is a future commitment rather than evidence that representation has already improved.

documents.title: Aurora Foods 2025 Inclusion and Accessibility Update
documents.text:
Aurora Foods published a fictional inclusion update covering recruitment, accessibility, and leadership. Job advertisements were reviewed to remove unnecessary degree requirements, and candidates could request sign-language interpretation, screen-reader-compatible assessments, or additional interview time.

The company partnered with two community organizations for a twelve-month recruitment pilot involving refugees and transgender job seekers. Forty-six people entered the pilot, 31 completed training, and 22 accepted permanent roles. The update reports participant counts but does not publish retention or pay data for the group.

Employees may voluntarily self-identify disability, race, ethnicity, and gender identity. Because response rates differed across locations, Aurora did not publish company-wide percentages for historically excluded groups. The document explicitly says that the absence of those percentages should not be interpreted as evidence of equal representation.

Two of the nine board members self-identified as members of historically excluded ethnic groups. No information was disclosed about executive leadership below the board, leaving a material gap in leadership evidence.

documents.title: Aurora Foods 2025 Environmental and Packaging Statement
documents.text:
The fictional Aurora Foods environmental statement reports operational electricity and packaging information. Meter records indicate that 72 percent of electricity used by the main processing facility came from contracted renewable sources in 2025. The statement excludes agricultural emissions and third-party transport, so it is not a complete product carbon footprint.

The company replaced a multilayer wrapper with a mono-material polypropylene wrapper for two product lines. A local recycling assessment classified the new wrapper as technically recyclable where flexible-plastic collection exists. Aurora notes that collection is not available in every consumer market and therefore does not describe the package as universally recyclable.

Paper cartons contained an average of 86 percent recycled fiber. The supplier certificate was valid through December 2026. Total packaging weight per product unit fell by 11 percent compared with the 2023 baseline.

Water use at the main facility declined by 8 percent per tonne of finished product, but the statement provides no farm-level water data. It also provides no independently verified life-cycle assessment.

documents.title: Aurora Dark Cocoa Bar Ingredient and Allergen Specification
documents.text:
The fictional Aurora Dark Cocoa Bar formulation lists cocoa mass, cane sugar, cocoa butter, sunflower lecithin, and natural vanilla flavor. The current ingredient specification contains no intentionally added animal-derived ingredient. The vanilla flavor supplier provided a composition declaration covering its carrier and processing aids.

The product is manufactured on equipment that also processes milk chocolate. The documented cleaning procedure includes a validated wash and a protein swab before vegan production begins. Nevertheless, the consumer label states that the bar may contain traces of milk because accidental cross-contact cannot be ruled out.

No animal testing is commissioned for the finished food product. The specification does not make claims about historical animal testing by every upstream ingredient manufacturer.

A formulation review was signed in February 2026 and is scheduled for renewal after any supplier change or after twelve months, whichever occurs first. This evidence applies to the named product rather than every product sold by the brand.

documents.title: Aurora Foods 2025 Worker Grievance and Wage Audit
documents.text:
An independent fictional labor audit reviewed payroll files, time records, interviews, and grievance logs at Aurora Foods. Auditors found that 14 temporary workers had not received the contractual night-shift premium for part of a six-week period. Aurora issued back pay and corrected the payroll rule, but the finding remains documented evidence of a wage-control failure.

Workers can submit complaints through an anonymous telephone line operated by an external provider, a locked box at the factory, or a named union representative. The log recorded 38 grievances during 2025. Thirty-four were closed, three remained under investigation, and one was withdrawn by the worker.

Interviewed workers generally knew at least one reporting channel, although night-shift workers were less familiar with the external telephone line. The corrective plan requires quarterly reminders in all shift meetings.

The audit found no evidence of recruitment fees in the sampled files. Because only a sample was reviewed, the report does not claim that fees could never occur anywhere in the supply chain.

documents.title: Aurora Foods 2025 Cocoa Origin and Traceability Report
documents.text:
Aurora Foods reports that the cocoa used in its fictional dark bar was purchased through three cooperatives in Ghana and one cooperative in Ecuador. Purchase records linked 78 percent of the annual cocoa volume to a named cooperative and district. The remaining 22 percent was documented only to country level.

Farm polygons were available for 61 percent of total volume. Satellite screening was performed for those mapped farms against the company's 2020 forest baseline. The report does not extend the screening conclusion to unmapped farms and describes deforestation traceability as partial.

Two Ghanaian cooperatives operated women-producer committees. Together they reported 318 registered members, but Aurora had not independently verified the committees' attendance records. Premium payments were recorded at cooperative level and could not be traced to individual farmers.

The Ecuadorian cooperative supplied chain-of-custody documents through December 2025. A scheduled renewal review was still pending when the report was published, so the document marks that evidence as needing an update.
